name: tortoise-orm-portable-per-statement-d498
instr:
Applications can place one portable deadline on an ORM operation instead of relying on driver-specific timeouts or cancelling the surrounding coroutine. The control follows the operation through query composition, persistence, prefetch, bulk work, and transactions while leaving subsequent database use safe.

`ExecutionOptions` from `tortoise.execution` is immutable and reusable; it accepts only an absent timeout or a finite positive non-boolean timeout, rejecting invalid controls before connection acquisition. One options instance establishes a non-renewing absolute deadline for the entire operation, and an exhausted deadline raises before acquiring another connection. Queryset clones and all model and executor reads and writes preserve that same control through filtering, annotation, values, update, delete, hydration, prefetch, and batching. Every controlled execution surface across `AsyncpgDBClient`, `PsycopgClient`, `MySQLClient`, `ODBCClient`, `SqliteClient`, `OracleClient`, and `MSSQL` transaction execution honors the remaining allowance and completes backend-appropriate cancellation and cleanup before returning or releasing resources, while Oracle and MSSQL retain their inherited ODBC and insert behavior. Successful controlled calls retain existing row conversion, affected-count, inserted-identifier, and transaction-wrapper behavior. `QueryExecutionTimeout` from `tortoise.exceptions` is an `OperationalError` exposing stable `operation` and `timeout` attributes and chain
